title: Precise, programmable replacement of large genomic regions in existing cells

concept.text: The envisioned capability is to replace a chosen stretch of a cell’s existing genome with a large, designed DNA sequence accurately and predictably. A replacement could encompass an entire gene together with nearby regulatory DNA, allowing coordinated changes to coding sequences, splicing elements and expression controls. The intended breadth includes multiple native genomic locations and diverse existing cell types, including cells that are not dividing. The supplied studies demonstrate important components of this capability in restricted settings; they do not establish the general capability.

Installing a landing site, inserting a large cargo and replacing a native genomic region are distinct operations. A landing site is a short sequence that enables an enzyme such as an integrase to insert DNA at that location. Successful cargo insertion does not by itself demonstrate removal and replacement of the original region. Conversely, replacement achieved through two editing steps and selection of mouse embryonic stem-cell clones does not establish an equivalent ability to rewrite mature tissues. The innovation requires control over the final genomic structure, its regulation and its biological function, beyond a positive integration measurement.

significance.text: Reliable large-region replacement would expand genetic engineering from changing individual mutations to rewriting whole functional units. Researchers could test coding and noncoding changes together, compare complete gene versions and construct more informative disease models. Taguchi and colleagues’ replacement of mouse regions with human counterparts, followed by studies of splicing, expression, function and disease-associated mutations, provides a concrete basis for this potential. Extending comparable control to diverse existing human cells would greatly broaden the experiments that could be performed.

A possible therapeutic consequence is a common replacement design for multiple pathogenic variants within one locus, provided that the replacement covers the relevant variants and restores the required biology. Such an approach could reduce the need to devise a separate edit for every mutation. That possibility remains conditional: gene dosage, the mechanism by which a variant causes disease, distant regulatory elements and tissue context can change what must be replaced. Sequence replacement alone does not establish a treatment, and delivery, toxicity, unintended changes and functional benefit would require validation for each application.

The genome-writing analogy has a biological limit: a correctly assembled DNA sequence is not sufficient evidence that the rewritten locus behaves as intended. Taguchi and colleagues note that distant regulatory regions may fall outside a replacement and that functional complementation depends on the gene. Their observation of reduced expression of a neighboring gene after one large replacement illustrates why surrounding genomic context matters. The revolutionary advance would therefore be dependable control of sequence and function together, rather than cargo size alone.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a broadly retargetable method that replaces large native regions at useful efficiencies across diverse primary cells, including nondividing cells, while preserving genomic integrity and intended function. Existing advances divide this challenge among different experimental systems: large-cargo integration after landing-site installation in cultured human hepatocytes, and native-region replacement through sequential editing and selection in mouse embryonic stem cells. Bringing these strengths together across many loci and mature cell types remains unestablished by the supplied evidence.

Delivery is a central engineering barrier because both the editing machinery and a large DNA donor must reach the relevant cells in a usable form. The L-PGI study attributes limitations with longer donors to delivery and identifies toxicity reduction as a development priority. DNA repair adds another source of variability: editing can produce insertions or deletions, unintended local structures, chromosome rearrangements or chromosome loss. A workflow that succeeds after selecting favorable stem-cell clones does not establish the same control in a mature tissue where edited and unedited cells coexist.

Precision must include the full replacement and its genomic surroundings. Correct boundaries can coexist with internal defects, extra donor copies, unintended donor integration elsewhere or damage to the other allele. Taguchi and colleagues report mutations in the non-knock-in allele and a neighboring-gene expression change, while the L-PGI authors state that they did not explore off-target editing. These findings make structural verification, genome-wide assessment and regulation central scientific requirements; they do not establish that either method inevitably produces unacceptable outcomes.

current_state.text: Nan, Chickering, Bartolome and colleagues published Ligase-mediated programmable genomic integration (L-PGI) on 10 December 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-67255-w. They report 14.4% on-target integration of a 30-kilobase transgene cargo in cultured primary human hepatocytes. The workflow first used pL-PGI to install a Bxb1 integrase landing site in PAH intron 1, followed by integrase-mediated cargo integration using a helper-dependent adenoviral donor. The supplied review identifies the cargo size in the Introduction and the integration measurement in the Results, where it was assessed by droplet digital PCR; the numerical result should not be attributed to the abstract. This is a targeted-integration result in a relevant primary-cell setting, rather than a demonstration of general native-region replacement or durable therapeutic function.

The adult-mouse experiments in the same study tested different endpoints. They measured average landing-site placement of 7.9% with pL-PGI and 2.5% with the dual PE-TB3 comparator, with droplet digital PCR described as a preliminary readout. A separate experiment measured insertion of 14 nucleotides. These results support in vivo installation of short sequences; they do not demonstrate the 30-kilobase cargo integration in adult mice. The study also leaves off-target editing unexplored and identifies further profiling and toxicity reduction as necessary development work.

Taguchi and colleagues published A scalable two-step genome editing strategy for generating full-length gene-humanized mice at diverse genomic loci on 14 January 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-67900-4. They report native-locus replacement with human DNA inserts ranging from 55 kilobases for CYBB to 205 kilobases for an APOBEC3 gene cluster. The method used two sequential CRISPR-assisted homologous recombination steps with drug selection in mouse embryonic stem cells, followed by generation of mice from engineered cells. This establishes large-region replacement in that experimental setting, including coding and noncoding DNA, but does not demonstrate direct replacement in existing mature tissues.

The Taguchi study extends beyond sequence insertion to biological readouts, including splicing, expression, function and disease-associated mutations. It also documents limits relevant to interpreting successful replacement: mutations can occur in the other allele, distant regulatory elements may be omitted, and functional complementation varies by gene. In the replacement exceeding 200 kilobases, neighboring Cbx7 expression was unaffected in lungs and spleens, whereas Cbx6 expression was reduced in lungs. These observations show why a structurally successful replacement still needs locus-specific biological assessment.

The supplied review had full main-article text for both studies, including saved publisher HTML and a main-paper PDF for Taguchi. Accordingly, the earlier account that restricted the Taguchi assessment to an abstract because of a blocked publisher page is superseded by the supplied review. Cookie-error parameters in saved URLs did not prevent retention of the full article text. The review did not inspect figure images, and the L-PGI review did not inspect linked supplements; Taguchi PDF prose was readable despite spacing artifacts. These limits constrain independent assessment of details beyond the reviewed text without negating the reported results.

Evidence boundary: these are dated published demonstrations, not a comprehensive assessment of the field through 1 November 2026. No bounded search or freshness record was supplied to establish whether later work expanded the demonstrated capability. The supplied studies therefore support substantial progress in restricted settings, while the broader innovation remains undemonstrated within this record.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently replace several native disease-relevant loci with large designed sequences in diverse primary human cell types, explicitly including nondividing cells. Prespecify the sequence-size range, minimum replacement efficiency, follow-up duration and acceptable unintended-change rates for each intended use. Those thresholds should reflect the application rather than an invented universal cutoff. Success across a finite test panel would establish demonstrated breadth across those conditions, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Large replacements across primary human cell types, including nondividing cells

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification: establish both genomic boundaries, the integrity of the entire replacement and its copy number, while checking whether unwanted native sequence remains. Measure local and genome-wide unintended changes, including rearrangements, damage to the other allele and ectopic donor integration. Evaluate the edited population as well as any selected clones, so that favorable clone selection does not obscure the distribution of outcomes. These are proposed requirements motivated by the structural and safety concerns in the supplied studies, not established consensus completion standards.
completion_criteria.label: Verify replacement integrity and unintended changes across edited populations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional and reproducibility checks: show intended expression, splicing, dosage and biological function over the prespecified follow-up period, including effects on relevant neighboring genes. Reproduce the results in independent experiments and laboratories, with explicit reporting of donor-to-donor variation, delivery conditions, cell survival and any selection required. If the intended use is treatment within an organ, add direct demonstrations of delivery and sustained benefit in that tissue; success in cultured cells or mice generated from selected stem cells would not alone meet that application boundary.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained replacement function reproduced across independent experiments and laboratories

related_concepts.text: Conceptual mapping to the supplied roster: GEN-01, A predictive, causal map of the genome’s regulatory code, would help determine which regulatory sequences a replacement must preserve or alter; GEN-03 supplies a way to construct and test those changes. GEN-11, Predicting genetic interactions across backgrounds and environments, addresses how a replacement’s effects vary with biological context. Genome writing could support those experiments, but accurate writing does not itself provide either predictive theory.

Conceptual mapping to the supplied roster: GEN-02, Design and construct complex eukaryotic genomes to specification, concerns genome-scale design and construction. GEN-03 focuses on replacing selected large regions within existing cells, a capability that could contribute to broader construction efforts without establishing whole-genome design or assembly. GEN-04, A retargetable delivery platform for genetic medicines across the body, addresses a major enabling requirement for therapeutic GEN-03 applications. Delivery to a tissue and precise replacement inside its cells remain distinct achievements.

Conceptual mapping to the supplied roster: GEN-05, General laws of environmentally induced, sequence-independent inheritance, concerns inherited effects that do not require DNA-sequence changes, whereas GEN-03 deliberately changes genomic sequence. GEN-06, Transferable clonal seed reproduction across major crops, and GEN-07, Predictably controllable inheritance in wild populations, concern reproductive and population-level inheritance. Large-region replacement might help engineer relevant systems, but it does not establish clonal seed reproduction or predictable population spread.

Conceptual mapping to the supplied roster: GEN-08, Reconstructing an organism’s cell divisions and histories from inherited molecular marks, aims to recover cellular histories; genomic writing could potentially install recording components without supplying the reconstruction capability. GEN-09, An autonomous, evolvable expanded genetic alphabet, changes the molecular alphabet available to heredity, while GEN-03 concerns writing large regions without requiring an expanded alphabet. GEN-10, A testable reconstruction of the origin and fixation of the genetic code, addresses an evolutionary explanation that engineered genomes might help investigate, but precise replacement would not itself resolve that history.

change_log.change: Preserved GEN-03’s identity and expanded its explanation to distinguish landing-site installation, large-cargo integration and native-region replacement.
change_log.reason: These are different experimental achievements; conflating them would overstate progress toward the proposed general capability.

change_log.change: Corrected the L-PGI result to 14.4% on-target integration of a 30-kilobase cargo in cultured primary human hepatocytes after landing-site installation, with the numerical evidence attributed to the Introduction and Results.
change_log.reason: The supplied review establishes the setting, staged workflow and ddPCR measurement, and corrects the earlier attribution to the abstract.

change_log.change: Added the adult-mouse landing-site measurements of 7.9% and 2.5% and separated them from the 14-nucleotide insertion and cultured-cell cargo experiment.
change_log.reason: The mouse findings concern short-sequence installation and do not establish in vivo integration of the 30-kilobase cargo.

change_log.change: Specified Taguchi’s 55–205-kilobase insert range, native-locus replacement, sequential CRISPR-assisted homologous recombination and drug selection in mouse embryonic stem cells.
change_log.reason: The reviewed full text provides more precise evidence than the earlier description of fragments exceeding 200 kilobases and clarifies the limits of extrapolation to mature tissues.

change_log.change: Replaced the abstract-only Taguchi access caveat with the review’s account of available full main-article text, while preserving uninspected figures, supplements and extraction limitations where applicable.
change_log.reason: The supplied review supersedes the earlier access account without implying additional inspection in this consolidation.

change_log.change: Integrated functional findings and biological limits, including neighboring-gene expression changes, other-allele mutations, distal regulation and gene-dependent complementation.
change_log.reason: These findings explain why sequence correctness, functional restoration and therapeutic suitability require separate assessment.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion demonstration to include prespecified quantitative thresholds, whole-replacement integrity, copy number, unintended integration, reproducibility and application-specific boundaries.
change_log.reason: Boundary verification alone is insufficient, and finite demonstrations establish breadth rather than universal performance.

change_log.change: Added distinct relationships to the supplied concept roster and retained the unresolved freshness limitation.
change_log.reason: Related capabilities should remain separate, and dated studies cannot establish a complete field assessment without a bounded search record.

unresolved_issues: No bounded freshness record establishes whether subsequent work changed the field’s demonstrated capabilities through 1 November 2026.
Sequence-size ranges, minimum efficiencies, follow-up periods and acceptable unintended-change rates remain to be specified for particular research or therapeutic uses.
The supplied evidence does not establish broadly reproducible large-region replacement across diverse mature human tissues, including nondividing cells.
The L-PGI study did not explore off-target editing; its integration measurement does not alone establish complete cargo integrity, durable function or therapeutic safety.
The supplied review did not inspect figure images or L-PGI linked supplements. Saved Taguchi supplementary artifacts do not by themselves establish that their contents were substantively reviewed.
The extent to which a common replacement can address multiple variants at a locus remains dependent on variant mechanism, dosage, regulatory coverage and tissue context.

brief.title: Precise replacement of long DNA stretches in living cells
possible: Researchers could replace a whole gene and its nearby controls within a living cell’s DNA, its genetic instructions. They could design coordinated changes across a long stretch and make the replacement behave predictably, including in cells that no longer divide.
why: Researchers could compare complete gene versions and build disease models that capture changes in both genes and their controls. A shared replacement could also offer a route to treating several disease-causing mutations in the same gene, reducing the need for a separate edit for each mutation.

sources.who: Angela X Nan, Michael Chickering, Christopher L Bartolome and colleagues
sources.showed: They inserted a designed DNA stretch of 30,000 DNA letters into cultured human liver cells after installing a short docking sequence for a DNA-inserting enzyme.
sources.quote: We introduce edits through delivery and ligation of a synthetic DNA donor to genomic nicks created with Cas9 nickase and report editing activity in cell lines, primary cell cultures, and adult mice via nonviral delivery.
sources.cited_for: Large DNA cargo can be inserted at a chosen site in cultured human liver cells.
sources.not_established: Insertion does not establish removal and replacement of the original DNA, lasting function or freedom from unintended changes.

sources.showed: They replaced mouse DNA with human counterparts in selected embryonic stem cells and generated mice. They measured gene activity, biological function and splicing, how cells assemble a gene’s message.
sources.quote: Humanized alleles generated using the developed method recapitulate human-like splicing isoforms and organ-specific gene expression while restoring essential functions in hematopoiesis, spermatogenesis, and survival.
sources.cited_for: Large replacements can include genes and their controls and support biological function in mice.
sources.not_established: Replacement in selected embryonic stem cells does not establish direct replacement in mature tissues; a neighboring gene’s activity also fell.

shown: Taguchi and colleagues achieved replacement with human DNA stretches reaching 205,000 DNA letters in mouse embryonic stem cells. Their work combines large replacements with biological tests in mice. Nan and colleagues demonstrated large DNA insertion in cultured human liver cells.
missing: A method that reliably replaces large native DNA regions across varied human cell types, including cells that do not divide, remains to be demonstrated.
Delivery of both the editing machinery and large replacement DNA into mature tissues still needs to work reliably with acceptable cell survival.
Whole replacements need population-wide checks for internal defects, extra copies, misplaced DNA and damage elsewhere.
Lasting gene function, effects on neighboring genes and reproducibility across laboratories remain to be established across these settings.

milestones.label: Large replacements work across human cell types
milestones.explanation: Large replacements would have to work at several disease-related sites in varied human cells, including nondividing cells, against preset performance limits. This would establish breadth across the tested conditions.

milestones.label: Complete replacements and unintended changes are measured
milestones.explanation: Checks would have to establish complete replacements, correct boundaries and copy counts, and unwanted DNA or damage across edited populations and selected cells. This would reveal outcomes that favorable cell selection can hide.

milestones.label: Lasting function is reproduced independently
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to reproduce lasting gene activity, message assembly and function, including neighboring-gene effects. Treatment within an organ would also require delivery and sustained benefit there.

uncertain: Useful replacement sizes, success rates, follow-up periods and acceptable unintended changes depend on the intended use.
Whether a shared replacement can address many mutations depends on disease mechanism, gene activity levels, regulatory coverage and tissue context.
